html:
The Secwépemc, or Shuswap, are an Interior Salish people of south central British Columbia. Their land, Secwepemcúl'ecw, covers the valleys of the Thompson, North Thompson and upper Fraser rivers and the Shuswap Lake country, centred on present Kamloops.

They wintered in pit houses dug into the ground and in summer moved to fish for salmon, hunt deer and elk, and gather roots and berries. The fur trade arrived with Simon Fraser in 1808 and Fort Kamloops in 1812, and the gold rushes of 1858 and the 1860s brought settlers and smallpox, which killed many in 1862. In 1910 Secwépemc chiefs joined others in the Memorial to Sir Wilfrid Laurier, asserting title to their land. In 2021 the Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc band announced likely unmarked graves at the Kamloops residential school, which led to a national reckoning in Canada. Their neighbours include the Syilx to the south, the Nlaka'pamux to the southwest and their own Esk'etemc community at Alkali Lake.
